And there vvas a certaine lord vvho{{ls}}e {{ls}}onne was {{ls}}icke at Capharnáum. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=47}}† He hauing heard that {{sc|Iesvs}} came from Ievvrie into Galilee, vvent to him, and de{{ls}}ired him that he vvould come dovvne & heale his {{ls}}onne. for he began to die. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=48}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore {{ls}}aid to him, Vnle{{ls}}{{ls}}e you {{ls}}ee {{ls}}ignes and vvonders, you beleeue not. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=49}}† The lord {{ls}}aith to him, Lord, come dovvne before that my {{ls}}onne die. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=50}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aith to him, Goe, thy {{ls}}onne liueth. The man beleeued the vvord that {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aid to him, and vvent. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=51}}† And as he vvas novv going dovvne, his {{ls}}eruants mette him: and they brought vvord, {{ls}}aying, That his {{ls}}onne liued. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=52}}† He a{{ls}}ked therfore of them the houre, vvherein he vvas amended. And they {{ls}}aid to him, That ye{{ls}}terday at the {{ls}}euenth houre the feuer left him. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=53}}† The father therfore knevv that it vvas in the {{ls}}ame houre vvherein {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aid to him, Thy {{ls}}onne liueth. and him {{ls}}elf beleeued and his vvhole hou{{ls}}e.⊣ {{verse|chapter=4|verse=54}}† This againe the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 2, 11.''}}* {{ls}}econd {{ls}}igne did {{sc|Iesvs}}, vvhen he vvas come from Ievvrie into Galilee.
